title: Computational Materials Science & AI
short: Atoms to components in silico: simulation, thermodynamics and machine learning for materials design.
overview: Computational materials science predicts structure and properties before a sample is made. Methods in use across the department include first-principles and molecular dynamics simulation, dislocation dynamics, phase-field and crystal plasticity modelling, computational thermodynamics and process simulation.

Data-driven methods — neural networks, evolutionary optimisation and materials informatics — are increasingly coupled to these models to screen alloys, battery materials and processing routes faster than experiment alone allows.
imageAlt: Composite of atomistic simulation snapshots and stress–strain results for dislocations and nanowires
